speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if you have been vomiting, especially if it looks like a green fluid? Have you noticed any blood in your stools or if your belly feels unusually hard when I touch it?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Since the abdomen is tender and distended, have you noticed any bilious (green) vomiting or any signs of constipation? I also need to check your vital signs and perform a digital rectal exam to see if there is blood at the exit.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray (to look for dilated loops and air-fluid levels). REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound (to evaluate for volvulus or malrotation).

text: Based on the X-ray showing dilated loops with absent rectal gas and your description of a tender, distended abdomen, I need to ask if the baby has passed any stool or gas since admission, and specifically if the stool has ever been "currant jelly" colored? Please also tell me if the abdomen is visible or feels rigid like a board.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.
